hook: An FBI 302 interview report documenting a multi-hour, multi-sensor UAP encounter at a classified US military facility in 2025, in which helicopter crews and ground observation posts simultaneously tracked orbs — including one described as 'super-hot' under FLIR — that split into two objects and outran helicopter pursuit over an estimated 20-mile distance.
why_it_matters: This document is notable for the depth of corroboration: sightings were confirmed across multiple sensors (FLIR, NVGs, naked eye) by multiple credentialed witnesses including senior US intelligence officials, military pilots, and ground-based LP/OP personnel — substantially reducing the likelihood of individual misidentification. The document records a consistent behavioral pattern of orbs sequentially flaring up and down over approximately 70 minutes and across multiple geographic locations, and the witnessing senior official explicitly states the orbs appeared to 'break off and pursue' military aircraft in the same airspace. As a formally recorded FBI 302, it carries the evidentiary weight of an official US government witness statement.
key_findings: An orb described as 'super-hot' under FLIR was observed hovering at ground level before splitting into two distinct objects and accelerating to a speed that helicopter CALL SIGN 1 could not match, traveling an estimated 20 miles before pursuit was abandoned.

The co-pilot observed under NVGs something emerge from the two split objects and travel in a separate direction at high rate of speed — corroborating the ground-based LP/OP account through an independent sensor.

Between approximately 2227 and 2257 hours, at least six distinct orb formation events were recorded across different compass bearings, each following the same behavior: orbs appearing oval-shaped and orange with white/yellow centers, flaring up one at a time in horizontal or triangle formations, then extinguishing in reverse sequential order.

The orbs closed to within ten feet of the helicopter (CALL SIGN 1), and Witness 1's closing comments state the orbs appeared to 'break off and pursue' military aircraft that were simultaneously operating in the airspace.

Pilots acknowledged they were recording but noted that most sightings were above the helicopter's rotor disk and outside the FLIR camera's angle of coverage, meaning the primary electro-optical sensor likely did not capture the most significant events.

legacy_program_connections.reasoning: This 2025 incident at a US military facility involving senior intelligence officials, multi-sensor tracking, and FBI documentation is precisely the category of event AARO was established to collect; it was released through the PURSUE initiative directly tied to congressional UAP reporting mandates.

The document was declassified and published on war.gov as part of the PURSUE release, which was a direct product of congressional UAP disclosure legislation requiring the government to publish UAP records.

The presence of a Listening Post/Observation Post equipped with FLIR and NVGs at a classified military facility, along with senior intelligence community witnesses, is consistent with NRO-adjacent sensor infrastructure, though the specific agencies are fully redacted.
